monthly_review.summary: This month shows a sharp drop in volume and frequency compared to last month, with pace and HR trending faster and higher despite minimal running — suggesting fatigue or reduced recovery capacity.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone 3 HR distribution jumped from 31% to 54% this month while Z1 dropped from 24% to 6%, indicating a significant shift toward higher-intensity effort despite only one run — likely reflecting accumulated fatigue or insufficient low-intensity recovery.

goal_tracker.message: You need 54.5 more km across 10 additional sessions in the next 28 days — averaging ~5.5 km per session — to match last month’s volume. Prioritize consistency: aim for 3–4 runs/week, including at least two Zone 2 sessions under 140 bpm.

insights.title: Efficiency declined despite faster pace
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency fell from 13.46 to 13.2 m/sec per bpm this month, even though average pace improved (+27 sec/km) and cadence rose (+2 spm). This suggests diminishing return on effort — likely due to insufficient Z1/Z2 volume compromising metabolic resilience.

insights.title: Overreliance on Zone 3
insights.body: Zone 3 effort now dominates 54% of this month’s single run vs 31% last month, while Z1 dropped from 24% to 6%. This imbalance risks aerobic base erosion and limits recovery capacity, especially given elevated avg HR (148 vs 140 bpm) on similar distances.

insights.title: Stride length increased but vertical oscillation rose
insights.body: Stride length improved from 68.77 cm (Jun 21) to 75.77 cm (Jul 1), yet vertical oscillation climbed from 7.7 to 8.1 cm — indicating less economical force application. Ground contact time dropped (314 → 311 ms), but the efficiency gain was offset by higher bounce.

insights.title: Aerobic TE remained high despite low volume
insights.body: Avg aerobic training effect held at 3.1 this month — identical to Jun 21, Jun 28, and Jul 1 runs — but achieved on just one 6.5 km run instead of distributed across multiple sessions. This suggests disproportionate physiological stress per run, increasing injury and fatigue risk.

recommendations.action: Do your next run as a strict 5 km Zone 2 effort at ≤135 bpm (based on last month’s avg HR of 140 and recent Z2 range), focusing on relaxed breathing and cadence ≥150 spm.
recommendations.reason: Z2 volume is critically low (only 19% this month vs 29% last month), and rebuilding aerobic capacity requires consistent sub-lactate-threshold work to lower avg HR and improve efficiency.

recommendations.action: Add a 20-minute post-run walk or easy spin immediately after your next moderate run to promote parasympathetic recovery — especially given elevated HR (148 bpm) and suppressed Z1 time (6%).
recommendations.reason: Z1 time dropped sharply (24% → 6%), signaling inadequate low-intensity recovery stimulus; active recovery can help restore autonomic balance without adding load.

recommendations.action: Perform a 3-minute cadence drill before your next run: 30 sec @ 160 spm, 30 sec @ 155 spm, 30 sec @ 150 spm, repeated 4x — using metronome app or Garmin cadence alert.
recommendations.reason: Cadence improved (+2 spm) but stride length gains coincided with rising vertical oscillation; controlled cadence practice reinforces neuromuscular efficiency and reduces bounce.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish foundational Zone 1–2 endurance through consistency, autonomic regulation, and movement economy — prioritizing time-in-zone over pace or distance.
suggested_sessions: 30-min Zone 1–2 mixed-effort walk/run (e.g., 5 min walk + 5 min easy jog x3)
